title: Tests use TestContext.Current.CancellationToken, not CancellationToken.None
statement: xUnit tests that call async APIs pass `TestContext.Current.CancellationToken` (captured once at the top of the test) rather than omitting the token or passing `CancellationToken.None`.
rationale: `TestContext.Current.CancellationToken` is wired to the test host's own cancellation (a run timeout, `dotnet test --cancel`, or CI's own deadline); a hung async call in test code will actually stop instead of hanging the whole suite. `GuidelineImpactAnalyzerTests` captures the token once and reuses it for every async call in the test.

good.code:
var cancellationToken = TestContext.Current.CancellationToken;
await File.WriteAllTextAsync(Path.Combine(root, "Sample.cs"), "class Sample { }\n", cancellationToken);
good.caption: Ambient test cancellation token captured and forwarded.

bad.caption: No cancellation token: a hang here outlasts the test run's own timeout.

changelog.summary: Initial rule, grounded in GuidelineImpactAnalyzerTests.cs. autofixable: true (mechanical token threading).
